sentences.text: Hydrolagus is a genus of marine fish found in the Atlantic, Indian, and Pacific Oceans, containing 22 recognized species such as the spotted ratfish and African chimaera.
These animals display an unusual appearance featuring pectoral fins that resemble wings, a dorsal fin ending in a point, and a long whip-like tail.
The genus was first described by T. N. Gill in 1862, with the oldest known fossils dating back to the Miocene epoch.
Fossil evidence from California includes remains from both the Miocene and Pliocene periods.
Some researchers suggest this lineage has undergone no changes in the last 150 million years.
Certain species inhabit depths of 736 meters in total darkness, detecting electromagnetic radiation from other creatures using specialized nerves on their bodies.
Taxonomically, the group belongs to the phylum Chordata, the subclass Holocephali, and the order Chimaeriformes.
It is classified within the family Chimaeridae, which serves as the parent group for the genus.
